questions: Did this walking problem begin suddenly, over minutes to hours?
Did it begin within the last 24 hours?
Has it been steadily worsening?
Have you had similar episodes before?
Do you feel the room spinning or yourself moving when you are still?
Do you feel faint or close to passing out when you stand or walk?
Do you have new weakness in either leg?
Do you have new weakness or clumsiness in either arm?
Do you have numbness or loss of sensation in either leg or foot?
Do you have difficulty knowing where your feet are without looking at them?
Do you have new double vision or loss of vision?
Do you have new slurred speech or difficulty finding words?
Do you have a severe or unusual headache?
Have you had a recent head injury?
Do you have new back pain?
Do you have loss of bladder or bowel control?
Do you have numbness around your groin or buttocks?
Do you have tremor, stiffness, or unusually slow movements?
Do you have difficulty coordinating your hands?
Do you have trouble swallowing?
Have you had fever or a recent infection?
Have you recently started or increased any medication?
Have you recently used alcohol, sedatives, cannabis, or other recreational drugs?
Do you have diabetes, vitamin B12 deficiency, thyroid disease, multiple sclerosis, or another neurological condition?
Do you have a history of stroke or seizures?
Is your walking noticeably better when you are alone or when you are distracted?
Does the pattern of your walking vary substantially from one attempt to another?
Are you able to move your legs normally when sitting or lying down?
Are you afraid that you will fall even when you are not physically unsteady?
Have anxiety or a major emotional or psychological stressor occurred shortly before this began?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Sporadic adult-onset cerebellar ataxia due to idiopathic degenerative cerebellar atrophy (non-inflammatory, non-paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration)

Alternative 1: Hereditary spinocerebellar ataxia, particularly an adult-onset dominant SCA such as SCA6

Alternative 2: Gluten-sensitive or anti-GAD-associated cerebellar ataxia

Alternative 3: Functional neurological gait disorder superimposed on organic cerebellar ataxia
